thread:
alex: quick heads-up — after the group-size refactor i pushed last night we're seeing a reproducible ~9% p50 latency regression on the AWQ int8 weight-only path for 4k tokens workloads. not catastrophic but above our noise.

marta: ugh. which change do you suspect? the group_size->grouping-mode split?

alex: yeah that's the main delta. i instrumented kernel selection and packing. looks like for some models we now pick the generic matmul kernel instead of the optimized int8-kvpack kernel when group_size % 16 != 0. the packing stage also increased CPU time.

kevin: can you paste the short profiler sample?

alex: sure — this is a single-request flame slice for long-chat (gpt-like) with kv cache warm:

```
# profiler slice (collapsed)
pack_weights_awq: 12.4ms
kernel_dispatch:    3.8ms  -> int8_generic_matmul
kv_kv_fetch:        0.6ms
kv_cache_copyout:   1.2ms
total_infer:        32.1ms
```

Before the refactor we had: 
```
pack_weights_awq: 5.7ms
kernel_dispatch:    2.5ms  -> int8_kvpack_optimized
total_infer:        29.5ms
```

marta: so pack_weights doubled. is that because we recompute group offsets instead of reusing precomputed packing maps?

alex: exactly. refactor made grouping decisions later in the pipeline so packing is done with a more generic codepath. we lost the fast path that assumes 16-aligned groups.

kevin: interesting — could also be cache-line misalignment if group_size changed per-layer. did you check memory traffic?

alex: i ran perf counters quickly. notable uplift in L1 misses during pack: L1-dcache-load-misses +55% vs baseline. suggests more scattery writes.

ryan: do we have a regression test in perf CI for int8 weight-only 4k token p50? ci-bot: Running perf-job/awq-int8-4k after merge. status: flaky (regression detected in 3/10 runs).

marta: ok plan: 1) add micro-bench that isolates pack_weights path + varying group_size alignments, 2) add kernel routing test that guarantees we still prefer int8_kvpack_optimized when compatible, 3) try revert of the late-binding grouping as an experiment.

kevin: i can add the microbench. quick sketch: iterate group_size in [8,12,16,24,32], measure pack_time, kernel_dispatch selection, and L1 miss rate. will run pinned on c5d-equivalent to reduce noise.

alex: thanks — also let's validate this isn't just the single-model edge-case. i saw similar but smaller effect on llama-2-13b and bigger on a narrower GPT variant. suggests model-specific per-layer group sizes matter.

marta: longer-term we should orthogonalize packing decisions vs kernel selection: packing should produce both aligned and fallback buffer shapes then route kernels based on capabilities without recomputing heavy metadata. that avoids rework.

kevin: agreed — also maybe we can move pack memoization earlier in model load time when model weights are static (for Dedicated/Private). for hosted we can amortize with a short-lived cache keyed by (model_version, group_size_profile).

ryan: one more thought: batching heuristics interact with this. if small batches + KV-cache hits create many short-lived pack ops, overhead multiplies. can we prioritize batch coalescing for weight-only runs?

alex: yes batching helps. i instrumented bursty traffic pattern and observed pack ops spike 3x when concurrent inflight requests > 8. suggested mitigation: 1) enable request-level packing cache keyed by weight_id+group_profile, 2) extend batching window by 2ms when pack miss rate is > X.

marta: action items:
- kevin: add microbench (pack micro vs group_size matrix) and push results to the thread (ETA EOD)
- alex: add a small change to kernel routing to prefer int8_kvpack_optimized when packable, add feature-flag for late-binding revert (small PR)
- ryan: add perf CI gate to run the AWQ int8 4k p50 smoke on PRs touching grouping/packing paths
- ci-bot: run the perf job on current tip and link flamegraphs

ci-bot: perf-job/awq-int8-4k - queued

kevin: starting microbench now, will attach JSON results and aligned heatmap (pack_time vs group_size)

alex: thanks all. if we can get the pack_time down to within 1.5x of baseline for non-16 alignments we're probably okay; otherwise we need to reintroduce the early-aligned fast path.

marta: also log for postmortem: calibration changes can change group_size profile when we switch AWQ/GPTQ modes — that might cause dynamic shifts in packing alignment even without code changes. watch eval regressions too. :eyes:

kevin: uploaded microbench results: pack_time heatmap attached (summary) — spike at group_size=12 and 24, L1 miss rate tracks pack_time. saving full traces to s3://redwood-perf/awq/pack-micro/1719112233.json

alex: uploaded a tiny PR toggling early-bound grouping for testing: r=kevin?

kevin: reviewing now. if it fixes perf in CI i'll land and follow up with a proper refactor to memoize packing maps.

ryan: i'll add the CI gate — might increase PR runtime but worth it to catch regressions early.

marta: nice. keep notes here and we'll sync in next infra standup. :thumbsup:
